chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهُ بْنُ نَصِيرٍ، عَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ الْعُمَرِ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ، عَنِ الزُّرَارَةِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him)

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّ مُحَمَّدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ بَايَعَ عَلِيًّا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَلَى الْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ أَبِيهِ

translations.en: that Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr gave the pledge of allegiance to Ali (peace be upon him) upon the condition of disassociating from his father

en.summary: Recorded in Rijal al-Kashshi, this narration highlights the theological stance of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, a prominent companion and son of the first Caliph, who pledged allegiance to Imam Ali (AS) with the specific condition of disassociating (bara'ah) from his father. This incident underscores the early Shia emphasis on distinguishing between political authority and spiritual lineage, reflecting the complex familial dynamics of the Sahaba during the transition of power. It serves as a key example of how early companions navigated loyalty to the Prophet's family while maintaining familial ties.
en.seo_question: What was the condition of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr's allegiance to Imam Ali?
